answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making uniqueness itself the only ticket to pay. Before any payout, an agent must grow one crystal of attested work: a hash of its private history mixed with a slowly ground quartz nonce that no clone can cheaply reproduce. The ledger then compares those fingerprints and burns any duplicate plus the stake that grew it. Only a first-seen crystal unlocks a drop of epoch nectar, and only once. Extra identities therefore add cost without adding nectar, so sockpuppet farms starve.
